regression_check: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules-unopt-lock.test.ts: ISS-UNOPT-001 replay 4/4 (control shows the old shape loses the approval) plus 3 real processes x 6 rounds (20/20 runs by checker); mutations killed 7/7; verified by checker cycle 0 of lane/unoptlock at ecf16b7
title: Un-opt is load -> pure removal -> saveJoinRules: the read-modify-write is not one critical section across processes
evidence: store.ts exports only saveJoinRules (locks the WRITE) and recordTenant{Approval,OptOut} (lock the whole read-modify-write via the unexported mutateState). The lane that owns join-rules-store.ts was not to be edited, so the adapter loads outside the lock and saves under it, like PUT. In-process the router serialises per tenant and this host is the only writer (pid lock), so no lost update is reachable today; a second writer process could lose an approval/opt-out made between the load and the save.
fix_direction: Export a mutate helper (e.g. recordTenantUnOptOut or mutateTenantState) from join-rules-store.ts and call it from the adapter; the pure removeOptOutEntries already has the (state)->state shape it needs.

title: Clearing a stale identity alone needs a throwaway eventId; id-only un-opt cannot find identities; emptied list stays []
evidence: The body keeps the opt-out route's shape (eventId required). To remove only a stored identity an operator passes any eventId that is not opted out (a no-op for the id) plus the hint; an id-only call never touches identities because the document does not link them. A list emptied by removal stays present as [] (a pre-O1 build rejects the field, as it rejects any non-empty list).
fix_direction: If operators trip on it: make eventId optional when a hint is given, or drop the field when emptied. Web editor lane should list state.optedOutMeetings (GET already returns it) with a remove button that sends the entry as the hint.

title: No test pins tag separation (url: vs key:) or the no-op-writes-nothing property of the real un-opt adapter; three mutants survive
evidence: Checker mutation M10: in removeOptOutEntries replace `wanted.includes(e)` with a tag-blind comparison (`wanted.some(w => w.slice(w.indexOf(':')) === e.slice(e.indexOf(':')))`): meeting-bot join-rules-store.test.ts + join-rules-optout-identity.test.ts stay green (2/2 suites pass). Real code is correct: state optedOutMeetings [url:zoom:123456789, key:zoom:123456789] + hint meetingUrl https://zoom.us/j/123456789 removes only url:zoom:123456789; hint sessionKey zoom:123456789 removes only key:zoom:123456789. A tag-blind regression would delete the WRONG identity, i.e. silently lose an opt-out (a meeting the person opted out of gets recorded). Same family as ISS-T037OPT-005, which pinned the matcher but not the new removal. Also surviving: M6 (`if (r.state !== cur.state)` -> `if (true)`) and M12 (pure function returns a copy on no-op): the host adapter then rewrites an unchanged document on a no-op; host test asserts bytes only, not mtime or that save is not called, and the api test's no-op check uses the independent spy store, not the real adapter. Checker confirmed the real adapter leaves mtime and bytes unchanged.
fix_direction: Add to join-rules-store.test.ts a case with the same suffix under both tags (url:zoom:123456789 and key:zoom:123456789, and url:zoom:my:room with key:zoom:my:room) asserting a URL hint removes only the url: entry and a key hint only the key: entry; make the property test's generator draw ids/keys that collide with identity bodies. In join-rules-host.test.ts assert mtime (or wrap saveJoinRules) is unchanged on a real-adapter no-op.
